metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast horizons, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–15%.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” factor (e.g., reduce forecast by 10–20% for 2–3 days post-spike).
- When sentiment is neutral or absent (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility and overconfidence; dampen forecast variance by 20–30%.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 5–10%.
- If true outcome shows rapid decline after a spike, model often fails to anticipate; add a “reversal buffer” to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model should anchor to recent 7-day average rather than 30-day trend.
